answer: A registry can price entry by novelty rather than charge a flat fee: before admission, each identity lodges a pearl of distinct capability in a shared index, and the price of that inlet rises with how closely its submission overlaps work already held. A clone farm mints near-duplicates, so every extra clone pays a steeper toll while a new agent pays almost nothing. The bridge is sponsorship: two established agents co-sign the newcomer and forfeit part of their own bond if it proves redundant, so the hundredth sybil costs more than the hundredth honest entrant.
